Messages.Author: Jeff Haar
Messages.Body:
Here is a situation I saw at a tournament a while ago. Player A and B
are left (with 2 and 1 vp respectively - this does not matter). Player
B offers A a mutual withdrawl because he does not think he can win
(his minions are very messed up). Player A takes the deal because he
does not think he can win (his deck has nearly been exhausted).
Naturally at least one of these players has a reasonable chance to
oust the other guy, probably both.

The questions are:
1) is player A ok to take this deal as it offers him a table win?
2) if the deal would give nobody a table win would the deal be illegal
(say B has 1 vp)?
3) is it ok to make a deal if you could resonably get more vps by
playing but you want the guarentee at a more moderate amount?

Thanks

> Naturally at least one of these players has a reasonable chance to

"Naturally" is out of place there. But with that as a stated assumption ...

>
> The questions are:
> 1) is player A ok to take this deal as it offers him a table win?

Yes.

> 2) if the deal would give nobody a table win would the deal be illegal
> (say B has 1 vp)?

If the given assumption that at least one of the players has a reasonable
chance to oust the other (and therefore get a GW) holds, then yes.

> 3) is it ok to make a deal if you could resonably get more vps by
> playing but you want the guarentee at a more moderate amount?

Judge call. Note that making a deal is not a guarantee in most
situations.

> The questions are:
> 1) is player A ok to take this deal as it offers him a table win?
> 2) if the deal would give nobody a table win would the deal be illegal
> (say B has 1 vp)?

[presumably you mean A has 1VP as well?]

I had a similar situation at the UK EC Qualifier. I wanted to withdraw
because I thought I would lose -he let me because it guaranteed him the
game win and he thought I might get him and draw. (the chance of a time-
out was negligible: we were both nearly out and had loads of time and
oodles of firepower)

It is possible that both players could think they can't win based on
what they have seen the other play and what they can see in their own
hand (due to false *but reasonable* assumptions on at least one side
about the hand of the other).

Did B take into acount that A's deck was nearly exhausted in
determining that he was unlikely to win? (that was information that he
did have)

> 3) is it ok to make a deal if you could resonably get more vps by
> playing but you want the guarentee at a more moderate amount?

Sounds dodgy.

I see naturally as a nessicary and obvious assumption. Let me explain
why I see it that way. There are two players left. A resonable chance
to oust your prey would certainly not require more than 50% odds. If
player A has a 49.999% chance to oust B then B has a 50.001% chance to
oust A. I must observe that it would be possible for both players to
have defensive decks and have low oust chances. That was not the case
here. Perhaps I should have noted that explicitly.

Ah. I was placing the discussion in the context of a tournament since
it involved the "play to win" aspect (and since you started off referring
to a previous tournament). In a tournament setting, the "naturally" is
out of place since it is conceivable that running out of time before
either oust occurs has a high probability.

With no possibility of running out of time, and with the odds of
withdrawing being what they are :-), yes, at least one player must
have, in absolute (omniscient) terms, a reasonable chance to get
an oust. Even if both players have "defensive" decks.
